title: Amazon EC2
full_title: Amazon EC2: L2 → L3 Interview Preparation
level: instance basics → storage, networking, scaling → hardening & incident response

sections.title: Mental model: what makes up an EC2 instance
sections.intro_md:
**EC2 = rent virtual servers.** You pick the image, size, network and storage; AWS runs it on the Nitro hypervisor. You're responsible for the OS and everything above it.

```
 ┌──────────────────────────── EC2 instance (i-0abc…) ────────────────────────────┐
 │  AMI (OS + software)  ── what boots                                            │
 │  Instance type m7g.large ── 2 vCPU Graviton, 8 GiB RAM, network up to 12.5 Gbps │
 │  Root EBS volume (gp3) + extra EBS volumes / instance store (ephemeral NVMe)    │
 │  ENI: private IP 10.0.11.20 (+ public IP / Elastic IP), Security Groups          │
 │  Instance profile → IAM role → temporary creds via IMDSv2 (169.254.169.254)      │
 │  User data (cloud-init script at first boot)                                     │
 │  Placement: Region → AZ → (placement group)                                     │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        ▲ managed via                 ▲ access via                ▲ observed via
   Launch Template + ASG       SSM Session Manager (no SSH)    CloudWatch agent, Inspector
```

**Instance lifecycle:**
```
 pending → running ⇄ stopping/stopped (EBS-backed: disk kept, no compute charge, public IP changes)
               │  ⇄ hibernate (RAM saved to EBS)
               └─► shutting-down → terminated (root EBS deleted by default; instance store always lost)
```

questions.title: What is EC2 and when do you choose it?
questions.short_md: Resizable virtual machines with full OS control. Choose EC2 when you need: specific OS/kernel/drivers, GPUs or special hardware, long-running stateful software (legacy apps, databases you self-manage), licensing tied to hosts, or maximum cost control at steady high load. Otherwise prefer managed compute (Fargate, Lambda, AgentCore) to avoid OS management.

questions.title: What is an AMI?
questions.short_md: Amazon Machine Image — template with root volume snapshot, boot settings, architecture (x86_64/arm64) and permissions. Sources: AWS (Amazon Linux 2023, Ubuntu, Windows), Marketplace, or your **golden AMIs** built with **EC2 Image Builder**/Packer (pre-hardened, patched, agents installed). AMIs are regional — copy to other regions for DR.

questions.title: Instance families and naming
questions.short_md: m7g.2xlarge │││   └── size (vCPU/RAM scale: large=2 vCPU … 2xlarge=8 vCPU) ││└── attribute: g = Graviton (ARM), i = Intel, a = AMD, d = local NVMe, n = network-optimised │└── generation (newer = better price/performance) └── family
questions.body_md:
```
 m7g.2xlarge
 │││   └── size (vCPU/RAM scale: large=2 vCPU … 2xlarge=8 vCPU)
 ││└── attribute: g = Graviton (ARM), i = Intel, a = AMD, d = local NVMe, n = network-optimised
 │└── generation (newer = better price/performance)
 └── family
```
| Family | For |
|---|---|
| **t** (burstable, CPU credits) | dev, low steady CPU — watch credit exhaustion (or unlimited mode) |
| **m** general purpose | web/app servers |
| **c** compute optimised | CPU-heavy (batch, encoding) |
| **r / x** memory optimised | caches, in-memory DBs |
| **i / d** storage optimised | high IOPS local NVMe |
| **g / p / inf / trn** accelerated | GPUs (inference/training), Inferentia, Trainium |

**Graviton** (ARM) typically gives ~20–40% better price/performance — need arm64 builds.

questions.title: User data and cloud-init
questions.short_md: Script/cloud-config that runs **once at first boot** (by default) as root: install packages, pull config, join cluster, start services. Keep it small (use golden AMIs for heavy setup), idempotent, no secrets in plain text (user data is readable via IMDS/console) — fetch secrets from Secrets Manager using the instance role.
questions.body_md:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
dnf install -y amazon-cloudwatch-agent
aws ssm get-parameter --name /app/prod/config --query Parameter.Value --output text > /etc/app/config.json
systemctl enable --now app
```

questions.title: Instance profile and IAM role
questions.short_md: An **instance profile** attaches an IAM role to an instance; the SDK automatically gets temporary, auto-rotated credentials from the **Instance Metadata Service**. Never store access keys on instances.

questions.title: IMDSv2 — why enforce it?
questions.short_md: IMDS (169.254.169.254) exposes metadata and **role credentials**. IMDSv1 is a simple GET → an **SSRF** bug in your app could fetch credentials (Capital One breach pattern). **IMDSv2** requires a session token obtained via a PUT with a hop limit — blocks most SSRF and open-proxy attacks.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** IMDS (169.254.169.254) exposes metadata and **role credentials**. IMDSv1 is a simple GET → an **SSRF** bug in your app could fetch credentials (Capital One breach pattern). **IMDSv2** requires a session token obtained via a PUT with a hop limit — blocks most SSRF and open-proxy attacks.

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600")
curl -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id
```
Enforce `HttpTokens=required` in launch templates (new default for many AMIs), set hop limit 1 (2 for containers on the host if needed), and enforce org-wide via SCP / account default.

questions.title: Launch templates and versioning
questions.short_md: Launch template = versioned config (AMI, type, SGs, IAM profile, user data, IMDS options, EBS, tags). ASGs reference a template **version** (`$Latest`/`$Default`/explicit). Versioning gives rollback and controlled rollouts (instance refresh).

questions.short_md:
| Type | Behaviour | Use |

| **Spread** | each instance on distinct hardware (max 7 per AZ) | small number of critical instances |
| **Partition** | groups on separate racks | Kafka, HDFS, Cassandra (rack awareness) |

questions.title: EBS vs instance store
questions.short_md:
| | **EBS** | **Instance store** |
|---|---|---|
| Type | network block storage | physically attached NVMe |
| Persistence | survives stop/start; snapshots to S3 | **lost on stop/terminate/hardware failure** |
| Scope | one AZ (attach to instances in that AZ) | that instance |
| Use | root disks, databases, durable data | caches, scratch, buffers, temp data |

questions.title: EBS volume types
questions.short_md: Encrypt by default (account setting, KMS). Performance limited also by **instance EBS bandwidth**.
questions.body_md:
| Type | Notes |
|---|---|
| **gp3** | default SSD; baseline 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s, provision more independently of size; cheaper than gp2 |
| **io2 Block Express** | very high IOPS, durability, multi-attach; critical databases |
| st1 / sc1 | throughput HDD / cold HDD for big sequential data |

questions.title: Snapshots and AMI protection
questions.short_md: EBS snapshots are incremental, stored in S3 (regional), copyable cross-region/account. Protect with: encryption (CMK), no public sharing (block public access for snapshots/AMIs), **Recycle Bin** retention rules for accidental deletes, AWS Backup plans with vault lock, lifecycle policies (Data Lifecycle Manager).

questions.title: Private IP, public IP, Elastic IP
questions.short_md: - **Private IP** — fixed for the instance's life, used inside the VPC. - **Public IP** — auto-assigned from AWS pool, **changes on stop/start**. - **Elastic IP** — static public IPv4 you own and can remap (charged; AWS bills public IPv4 addresses hourly). Prefer load balancers/DNS over EIPs for apps.

questions.title: Security groups on EC2
questions.short_md: Stateful virtual firewall on ENIs: allow rules only, reference other SGs (e.g., app SG allows 8080 from ALB SG). No SSH from `0.0.0.0/0`. Outbound restricted where possible.

questions.title: Key pairs vs better access options
questions.short_md: Key pairs = SSH public key injected at launch (private key download once). Problems: key sharing, rotation, open port 22. Better: **SSM Session Manager** (no inbound ports, IAM-controlled, sessions logged to S3/CloudWatch), **EC2 Instance Connect** (short-lived keys pushed via API), EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint for private instances.

questions.title: Network performance constraints
questions.short_md: Each instance type has network bandwidth limits ("up to" = burst with credits), packets-per-second limits, EBS bandwidth limits, and connection tracking limits (security groups track connections — very high connection counts can hit `conntrack` allowances). Enhanced networking (ENA) is standard on modern types. Check `NetworkIn/Out`, ENA allowance-exceeded metrics (`bw_out_allowance_exceeded`, `conntrack_allowance_exceeded`).

questions.title: EC2 status checks vs application readiness
questions.short_md: - **System status check** — AWS hardware/network problem → stop/start moves to new host (or auto-recover). - **Instance status check** — OS problem (kernel panic, network misconfig) → reboot/fix. - **Attached EBS status check**. - **ELB / ASG health checks** — is the **application** responding? An instance can pass EC2 checks while the app is dead → configure ASG `HealthCheckType=ELB` so it replaces instances failing the app health check.
questions.body_md:
- **System status check** — AWS hardware/network problem → stop/start moves to new host (or auto-recover).
- **Instance status check** — OS problem (kernel panic, network misconfig) → reboot/fix.
- **Attached EBS status check**.
- **ELB / ASG health checks** — is the **application** responding? An instance can pass EC2 checks while the app is dead → configure ASG `HealthCheckType=ELB` so it replaces instances failing the app health check.

questions.title: On-Demand vs Savings Plans vs Reserved vs Spot
questions.short_md:
| Model | Discount | Commitment | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **On-Demand** | 0% | none | spiky, short-term, unknown |
| **Savings Plans** (Compute / EC2 Instance) | up to ~66–72% | $/hour for 1 or 3 yrs; Compute SP also covers Fargate & Lambda | steady baseline |
| **Reserved Instances** | similar | specific instance type/region (capacity reservation option) | legacy/specific needs |
| **Spot** | up to ~90% | none; **can be reclaimed with 2-minute notice** | fault-tolerant batch, CI runners, stateless workers |
| On-Demand Capacity Reservations | 0% | reserve capacity in an AZ | guaranteed capacity (e.g., events, GPUs) |

questions.title: Using Spot safely
questions.short_md: Diversify instance types/AZs (ASG mixed instances policy, `price-capacity-optimized` allocation), handle interruption notices (EventBridge / IMDS `spot/instance-action`) to drain work, checkpoint jobs, keep an on-demand base capacity, capacity rebalancing.

questions.title: Auto Scaling groups
questions.short_md: An ASG keeps a fleet between min/max/desired across AZs, replaces unhealthy instances, registers with target groups, and scales by policies.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** An ASG keeps a fleet between min/max/desired across AZs, replaces unhealthy instances, registers with target groups, and scales by policies.

```
 ASG (min 2, desired 3, max 10, subnets in AZ-a/b/c, launch template v12)
   ├─ target tracking: CPU 50%  or ALB RequestCountPerTarget 1000
   ├─ health check type: ELB, grace period 300 s
   ├─ instance refresh: rolling replace to new template version (min healthy 90%)
   ├─ lifecycle hooks: on launch (bootstrap) / on terminate (drain, upload logs)
   └─ warm pool: pre-initialised stopped instances for faster scale-out
```

questions.title: Scaling policies
questions.short_md: Target tracking (simplest), step scaling, scheduled, **predictive scaling** (ML forecast for daily cycles). Scale on the metric that reflects load (requests per target, queue depth per instance) rather than only CPU.
questions.body_md: Target tracking (simplest), step scaling, scheduled, **predictive scaling** (ML forecast for daily cycles). Scale on the metric that reflects load (requests per target, queue depth per instance) rather than only CPU.

questions.title: Graceful termination and draining
questions.short_md: Scale-in/instance refresh → ALB **deregistration delay** drains connections → **lifecycle hook** (`autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING`) gives time to finish jobs/flush logs → instance terminates. Use instance **scale-in protection** for instances doing critical work. Apps should handle SIGTERM on shutdown.

questions.short_md: ECS-optimised AMI (or Bottlerocket), ASG **capacity provider** with managed scaling + managed termination protection, mixed instances (on-demand base + Spot), instance draining on scale-in, ENI trunking for awsvpc density, IMDSv2 with hop limit restrictions so tasks use **task roles** not the instance role, CloudWatch/Container Insights, or simply use **ECS Managed Instances** to let AWS handle this.

questions.title: Deploying new versions on EC2
questions.short_md: Options: in-place (CodeDeploy agent, Ansible) — simple but mutable; **immutable**: bake new AMI → new launch template version → instance refresh or blue/green ASG behind the ALB → rollback by reverting template version. Immutable infra is safer and reproducible.

questions.short_md: Golden AMIs rebuilt regularly (Image Builder pipelines with CIS hardening), **SSM Patch Manager** with maintenance windows and patch baselines, **Inspector** vulnerability scanning, minimal packages, IMDSv2, no SSH (Session Manager), encrypted EBS, least-privilege instance role, CloudWatch agent for logs/metrics, GuardDuty, AWS Config compliance rules.

questions.title: Systems Manager (SSM) toolbox
questions.short_md: Session Manager (shell access), Run Command (run scripts across fleets), Patch Manager, State Manager (enforce config), Parameter Store, Inventory, Automation runbooks (e.g., isolate instance). Requires SSM agent + instance role with `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` + network path (endpoints or NAT).

questions.title: Monitoring EC2
questions.short_md: Default metrics: CPU, network, disk I/O, status checks (5-min; 1-min with detailed monitoring). **Memory and disk space need the CloudWatch agent.** Alarms: status check failed (auto-recover action), CPU credit balance (t-family), disk usage, app metrics.

questions.title: Incident response for a compromised instance
questions.short_md: 1. **Contain:** don't terminate (evidence). Replace SGs with an isolation SG (no inbound/outbound), detach from ASG/target group (set standby / protect from scale-in), revoke role sessions (deny policy with `aws:TokenIssueTime` condition). 2. **Preserve:** EBS snapshots, memory capture if possible, collect logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty findings). 3. **Investigate:** what was accessed with the role credentials (CloudTrail), lateral movement. 4. **Eradicate & recover:** rebuild from a clean golden AMI, rotate any secrets the instance could read, patch root cause. 5. **Lessons learne…
questions.body_md:
1. **Contain:** don't terminate (evidence). Replace SGs with an isolation SG (no inbound/outbound), detach from ASG/target group (set standby / protect from scale-in), revoke role sessions (deny policy with `aws:TokenIssueTime` condition).
2. **Preserve:** EBS snapshots, memory capture if possible, collect logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty findings).
3. **Investigate:** what was accessed with the role credentials (CloudTrail), lateral movement.
4. **Eradicate & recover:** rebuild from a clean golden AMI, rotate any secrets the instance could read, patch root cause.
5. **Lessons learned:** automate with SSM Automation / GuardDuty → EventBridge → Lambda.

questions.title: Instance is running but unreachable (SSH or app)
questions.short_md: Path check: correct IP (public IP changed after stop/start?) → route table (public subnet → IGW; private → via bastion/SSM) → **security group** inbound rule for your IP/port → NACL (stateless — ephemeral ports outbound) → OS firewall → service actually listening on `0.0.0.0:port` (`ss -lntp`) → status checks / system log / EC2 serial console for boot issues. Use **Reachability Analyzer** to test the network path.

questions.title: CPU stays low but endpoint latency spikes
questions.short_md: Not CPU-bound — look at: t-instance **CPU credits** exhausted (throttled — CPU metric may look capped), EBS throughput/IOPS limits or burst balance (gp2), network bandwidth/PPS/conntrack allowances exceeded, memory pressure/swap, GC pauses, thread/connection pool exhaustion, downstream dependency latency (traces), DNS resolution issues.
questions.body_md: Not CPU-bound — look at: t-instance **CPU credits** exhausted (throttled — CPU metric may look capped), EBS throughput/IOPS limits or burst balance (gp2), network bandwidth/PPS/conntrack allowances exceeded, memory pressure/swap, GC pauses, thread/connection pool exhaustion, downstream dependency latency (traces), DNS resolution issues.

questions.title: ASG keeps replacing instances in a loop
questions.short_md: ELB health check failing because the app needs longer to start than the **health check grace period**, user data failing (check `/var/log/cloud-init-output.log`), wrong health check path, missing IAM permissions to fetch config/secrets at boot, AMI broken. Suspend `ReplaceUnhealthy` temporarily to debug.

questions.title: Migrate a legacy EC2 API to ECS
questions.short_md: Containerise (Dockerfile, externalise config/secrets, logs to stdout, stateless — move local files to S3/EFS, sessions to Redis), build in CI, deploy ECS service behind the same ALB (new target group), shift traffic with weighted listener rules (10% → 100%), monitor, keep EC2 ASG for rollback, then decommission.

questions.title: Spot instances interrupted mid-job
questions.short_md: Handle 2-minute notice (stop taking work, checkpoint), make jobs resumable/idempotent, queue-based work distribution so another worker picks up, diversify instance types, keep on-demand base.
questions.body_md: Handle 2-minute notice (stop taking work, checkpoint), make jobs resumable/idempotent, queue-based work distribution so another worker picks up, diversify instance types, keep on-demand base.

questions.title: Reduce EC2 costs
questions.short_md: Right-size (Compute Optimizer), Graviton, Savings Plans for baseline, Spot for flexible workloads, auto scaling + schedules (turn off dev at night), gp3 instead of gp2, delete unattached EBS/old snapshots/unused EIPs, VPC endpoints to cut NAT data charges.
